'''Kristi Lynn Kiick''' (May 19, 1967 – January 2, 2026) was an American academic who was the Blue and Gold Distinguished Professor of Materials Science and Engineering at the [[University of Delaware]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> She studied polymers, biomaterials and hydrogels for drug delivery and regenerative medicine. She was a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]], and of the [[National Academy of Inventors]]. She served for nearly eight years as the deputy dean of the college of engineering at the [[University of Delaware]].

==Early life and education==
Kristi Kiick was born in [[Easton, Pennsylvania]], on May 19, 1967.<ref name="" :0''="">{{cite web |title=Kristi L. Kiick |url=https://rtfoard.com/obituary/kristi-l-kiick/ |accessdate=August 11, 2026}}</ref> She first became interested in a career in the chemical sciences when she was at high school.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.rsc.org/py/2012/12/06/author-of-the-week-prof-kristi-l-kiick/|title=Author of the Week: Prof. Kristi L. Kiick – Polymer Chemistry Blog|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> She studied chemistry at the [[University of Delaware]], from which she graduated [[summa cum laude]] as a Eugene du Pont memorial distinguished scholar.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.udel.edu/udaily/2019/december/kristi-kiick-national-academy-of-inventors-engineering/|title=Kristi Kiick honored for inventions {{!}} UDaily|website=udel.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> She was a Master's student at the [[University of Georgia]], where she was awarded a [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) [[predoctoral fellow]]ship, and joined [[Kimberly-Clark]] as a research scientist in 1992.<ref name=":1" /> Kiick returned to academia for a second master's degree in [[polymer science]] and engineering at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref name=":1" /> She completed her doctoral research at the [[California Institute of Technology]], as a National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate (NDSEG) fellow.<ref name=":1" /> She completed her PhD from the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] on templated macromolecular synthesis in 2001 under the supervision of [[David A. Tirrell]],<ref name=aphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|title=Expanding the scope of templated macromolecular synthesis in vivo: The incorporation of methionine analogues into proteins in vivo by altering the methionyl-tRNA synthetase activity of a bacterial expression host|year=2001|first=Kristi Lynn|last=Kiick|url=https://scholarworks.umass.edu/dissertations/AAI3012149|website=umass.edu|publisher=University of Massachusetts Amherst|oclc=931602667|archive-date=2024-04-06|access-date=2020-01-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240406181510/https://scholarworks.umass.edu/dissertations/AAI3012149/|url-status=dead}}</ref> prior to starting her faculty position at the [[University of Delaware]] in 2001.

==Research and career==
Kiick designed polymer nanostructures for targeted therapies and hydrogel matrices for [[regenerative medicine]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://sites.udel.edu/kiickgroup/research/|title=Research {{!}} Kiick Research Group|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> She made use of [[Biomimetics|biomimetic]] self-assembly, [[bioconjugation]] and biosynthesis.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bioengineering.qmul.ac.uk/events/?eid=3709|title=Events: Institute of Bioengineering, Queen Mary University of London|website=bioengineering.qmul.ac.uk|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> In particular, Kiick worked on polymer-peptide [[Macromolecule|macromolecular]] structures that can engage cellular targets. These include the use of [[polyethylene glycol]] (PEG) in [[click chemistry]] to form [[hydrogels]] that degrade selectively in response to molecules present in tissues and [[extracellular matrix]].<ref name=":3" /> Kiick showed that it is possible to selectively release small molecule cargo with a tuned release for applications in targeted drug-delivery and vascular grafts.<ref name=":3" /> She developed [[resilin]]-like polypeptides (RLP), elastomeric materials that can be cross-linked using small molecules, as well as hydrogels that contain nanoparticles for targeting tumors and inflammatory conditions.<ref name=":2" /> [[Resilin]] is a primary elastomeric protein that is found in insects, and helps them to jump long distances and produce sound.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2013/08/09/210508780/flexible-insect-protein-inspires-super-rubber|title=Flexible Insect Protein Inspires Super Rubber|website=NPR.org|date=9 August 2013 |language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

She joined the faculty at the [[University of Delaware]] in 2001 and earned the rank of associate professor in 2007. In 2011, Kiick was promoted to the rank of professor of materials science and engineering and also named deputy dean of the [[University of Delaware]]’s college of engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimbe.org/kristi-kiick-named-deputy-dean-college-engineering-effective-aug-1/|title=Kristi Kiick Kristi Kiick Named Deputy Dean of College of Engineering Effective Aug. 1 |website=aimbe.org|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> In 2019–2020, she was awarded a Leverhulme Visiting Professorship from the [[Leverhulme Trust]] and a Fulbright Scholarship from the [[Fulbright Program]] to the [[University of Nottingham]], to develop protocols for fabricating bioelastomeric materials.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fulbright.org.uk/about-us/meet-our-fulbrighters/2019-20-us-uk-fulbright-award-grantees/2019-20-american-fulbright-scholar-award-grantees|title=2019-20 American Fulbright Scholar Award grantees {{!}} US-UK Fulbright Commission|website=fulbright.org.uk|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22|archive-date=2020-02-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217140312/http://www.fulbright.org.uk/about-us/meet-our-fulbrighters/2019-20-us-uk-fulbright-award-grantees/2019-20-american-fulbright-scholar-award-grantees|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.udel.edu/udaily/2019/august/kristi-kiick-fulbright-leverhulme-united-kingdom-nottingham/|title=International scholarship in materials {{!}} UDaily|website=udel.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> 

==Personal life and death==
Kiick was married with two children.<ref name=":0" /> She died on January 2, 2026, at the age of 58 after a battle with [[leiomyosarcoma]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>[https://rtfoard.com/obituary/kristi-l-kiick/ Kristi L. Kiick]</ref>

After retiring from the University of Delaware, Kiick worked to establish funding for a UD College of Engineering program supporting science education outreach.  Entitled the Kristi Kiick Engineering Education Ecosystem (E3) Support Fund, the fund remains active and continues to accept contributions in her memory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AlumnIQ |url=https://ud.alumniq.com/p/giving/to/26WBJ |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=ud.alumniq.com}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Her awards and honours include:

* 2003 [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]]
* 2004 [[University of Delaware]] Francis Alison Young Scholar Award 
* 2010 [[University of Minnesota]] Etter Memorial Lectureship in Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www1.chem.umn.edu/news/news.lasso?serial=41|title=Department of Chemistry|website=chem.umn.edu|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2012 [[University of Delaware]] Trabant Award for Women's Equity<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.udel.edu/women/awards-honors/|title=Awards & Honors {{!}} Women's Caucus|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2014 [[University of Southern Mississippi]] Bayer Distinguished Lectureship<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://old.polyacs.org/524.html|title=POLY - What's New|website=old.polyacs.org|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2014 Elected a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS)
* 2014 Elected a fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (AIMBE)
* 2015 [[University of Southern Mississippi]] Covestro Distinguished Lectureship<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usm.edu/polymer-science-engineering/covestro-lecture-series.php|title=The Covestro Lecture Series {{!}} School of Polymer Science and Engineering {{!}} The University of Southern Mississippi|website=www.usm.edu|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
* 2019 [[Fulbright Program]] Scholar<ref name=":4" />
* 2019 Elected a [[fellow]] of the [[National Academy of Inventors]]<ref name=":1" />
* 2024 [[University of Delaware]] Medal of Distinction<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tosh-Morelli |first=Vicky |date=2024-09-27 |title=Engineering faculty honored with Medals of Distinction |url=https://engr.udel.edu/news/2024/09/college-of-engineering-faculty-honored-with-medals-of-distinction/ |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=UD College of Engineering |language=en-US}}</ref>
